title: System One game spec
description: Contract 1. The only per-game design work in System One: what the AI sees and what it can do.

features.description: Fixed feature slots. Every slot is normalized to [-1,1] by the game before the brain sees it. Order is part of the spec hash: reordering invalidates every trained brain.

actions.description: Discrete intents. The game maps each index to its own steering, aiming, and animation. Continuous control is deliberately not in the contract because it does not transfer between games.

contexts.description: Moods the gate can select. A gated brain needs one weight row set per context.

inputs.description: Names of the gate's ramp inputs. These are derived from the feature vector by the game, so they cost no extra integration.

thresholds.description: Defaults for the trained brain: [execute_pressure, execute_advantage, save_below, hold_below]. Trained values in the .s1b override these.

archetypes.description: Roles. Each gets a bias row so the same brain plays an entry and a sniper differently.

reward.description: Shaping weights for the trainer. Recorded in the spec so the reward is reviewable, not buried in code.

budget_bytes.description: Hard cap on brain size. The pipeline refuses to publish a brain that exceeds it. Tiers: ~1 KB linear, ~4 KB with two hidden ramps, ~16 KB for a small MLP.

sim.description: Optional. Only needed by the headless trainer and the browser arena; a Unity game can omit it.
